summary: OUTPOST ZERO is a browser-based educational space survival simulator for children ages 7–12. Players become commanders of humanity's research outpost on the Moon or Mars, managing five interdependent life-support resources: Oxygen, Electrical Power, Water, Food, and Radiation Shielding. Every decision carries a real engineering trade-off — saving electricity today may reduce oxygen recycling tomorrow. The game integrates real NASA open data including live solar flare alerts from NASA DONKI, Mars rover photographs from Curiosity, Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), and astronaut health research from NASA OSDR. A speed-of-light communication delay mechanic teaches players why astronauts on Mars must make life-or-death decisions autonomously without waiting 22 minutes for Earth's reply. The Cadet Learning Center features 10 interactive space science lessons and quizzes. Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Recharts for real-time telemetry visualizations.
details:
OUTPOST ZERO is a fully functional, turn-based browser game built with React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and Framer Motion. The game presents players with 15+ randomized mission events drawn from real spaceflight challenges: micrometeoroid hull impacts, Martian dust storms blocking solar panels, oxygen scrubber failures, and deep-space communication blackouts.

The simulation engine tracks five primary resources with mathematical interdependence — a decision to run the greenhouse photoperiod boosts food production by +10 units per sol but consumes -6 water and -5 electrical power. Players can toggle tactical subsystem overrides including Low-Power Conservation Mode, Life-Support Scrubber Overdrive, Electromagnetic Shield Overcharge, and Autonomous Rover Geological Survey.

Five NASA APIs are integrated with graceful offline fallback caching: NASA DONKI (solar flares and CMEs), Mars Rover Photos API (Curiosity raw imagery), NASA APOD, and NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR). All data is clearly labeled as REAL NASA DATA vs SIMULATED GAME DATA.

A realistic speed-of-light radio delay mechanic simulates Earth-Moon (1.3 seconds) and Earth-Mars (3–22 minutes one-way) communication latency, teaching children why astronauts must make autonomous emergency decisions.

When missions fail, a constructive Mission Failure Diagnostic explains the exact survival rule breached, with Recharts telemetry graphs showing resource trajectories. Three difficulty levels (Explorer, Commander, Mission Expert) and randomized events ensure high replayability. LocalStorage provides save/resume and career statistics. Fully open-source under the MIT License.

Live Demo: https://spectacular-tanuki-f1edb2.netlify.app
